{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.2 (HDI / Company Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.2 — 19 findings (4 critical, 6 high, 8 medium, 1 low)

## Executive summary

The commercial architecture of this Agreement is broadly acceptable to us — fees are a pure revenue share with no minimum commitment, assignment is unrestricted and runs to our successors, the exclusivity we grant is category- and term-limited with performance exits, there is no non-solicit binding us, the only "no less favorably" undertaking runs in our favour, and New York law is our preferred governing law. Our no-cause exit on 90 days' notice sits at the fallback.

The problem is what the Agreement does not say. There is no indemnification language of any kind, no limitation of liability or damages exclusion, no allocation of ownership over the Site, our Content or the customer/order data HDI collects, no performance warranty, no post-termination transition or data-return obligation, and no insurance covenant. HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site and processes customer order data, so these gaps are not academic: absent redlines, HDI would own the Site and its code with no licence back to us, we would have no remedy for defective performance, no IP-infringement protection, and no right to recover our data on exit. We have inserted the standard provisions in each case.

One affirmative term is materially off-market: the Section 4.2 Termination Payment is a one-way, uncapped payment by the Company alone (50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000), payable even on a no-cause exit, with no reciprocal obligation on HDI. We have capped it at three months' fees. Four further items (licence scope, non-compete breadth, audit frequency, non-renewal notice window) require narrow, minimal edits.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 5.4 (Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a…) |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 1.4 (HDI shall provide the Company with access to…) |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Missing | § 5.4 (Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a…) |
| 4 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 (HDI shall provide the Company with access to…) |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 1.4 (HDI shall provide the Company with access to…) |
| 6 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Deviation | § 5.4 (Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a…) |
| 7 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 5.4 (Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a…) |
| 8 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant (fallback) | § 5.4 (Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a…) |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (fallback) | § 1.4 (HDI shall provide the Company with access to…) |
| 10 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5.4 (Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a…) |
| 11 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Missing | § 1.4 (HDI shall provide the Company with access to…) |
| 12 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 (HDI shall provide the Company with access to…) |
| 13 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Deviation | § 1.4 (HDI shall provide the Company with access to…) |
| 14 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 5.4 (Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a…) |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 1.4 (HDI shall provide the Company with access to…) |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 1.4 (HDI shall provide the Company with access to…) |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 5.4 (Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a…) |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 (Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a…) |

### Notes on the deviations and gaps

- **INDEMN (missing).** No indemnification, defence or hold-harmless language appears anywhere. We inserted the standard HDI indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with a notice-and-control procedure; the Company gives no reciprocal indemnity and we have left that as is.
- **IP (deviation).** The Agreement never allocates ownership. Editorial control (5.2), merchant-of-record status (5.3) and the narrow Marks licence (6.1) do not cure this, and the Section 1.4 access right dies with the term. We inserted Company ownership of Content, Site deliverables and customer data, with HDI retaining its generic tools and granting a perpetual royalty-free licence.
- **LOL-CAP (missing).** Section 9 contains only authority representations and Section 10 is boilerplate; both parties face unlimited direct and consequential damages. We inserted a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, with indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap.
- **LD (deviation).** Section 4.2 imposes a one-way, uncapped payment on the Company (50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000), payable even on a no-cause exit, while HDI owes nothing if it terminates (4.2(b)). That far exceeds the fallback of an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees; we capped it at three months' fees as the sole termination amount.
- **LICENSE (deviation).** The Section 1.4 grant runs to the Company alone with no coverage for affiliates or contractors and no path to add them, failing the fallback. It is not expressed as revocable at HDI's discretion, so this is not walk-away. We added affiliates, contractors and successors.
- **NONCOMPETE (deviation).** Section 6.1 restrains us from "any project similar to the Site" for Deerskin Products or "products substantially similar" from "companies similar to" the named competitors — an open-ended field-of-use restraint that fails the fallback's named-competing-product requirement; the 6.2 closeout carve-out does not cover internal development or acquisitions. Term-only, so not walk-away. We narrowed it to a competing Deerskin-branded consumer site with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs.
- **WARRANTY (deviation).** No warranty that HDI's development, hosting and operation will be performed competently or that the Site will conform to approved specifications; the 1.6 launch deadline is a delivery milestone, not a warranty. We inserted a workmanlike / conformance / no-malicious-code warranty with a re-performance, repair or refund remedy. There is no disclaimer to carve out.
- **TRANSITION (missing).** Article 4 addresses only term, notice and the Termination Payment; Section 10.7 preserves only Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10, so nothing requires return of our Content, user information or order data, migration assistance or deletion. We inserted a new Section 4.3 (six months' assistance at HDI's rates, return within 30 days, certified deletion).
- **AUDIT (deviation).** Section 3.4 already meets our position on notice (30 days), business hours, scope (payment-calculation records only), cost (HDI bears it) and no system access, but has no frequency limit; the fallback requires once per year. We added a once-per-12-months cap. The absence of an independent-auditor requirement is noted, not flagged.
- **RENEWAL (deviation).** Annual auto-renewal with a 90-day non-renewal window exceeds the fallback of 60 days. We shortened the Company's window to 30 days and left HDI at 90 so HDI cannot exit on shorter notice. The 12-month renewal term is acceptable and there is no price uplift (revenue share), so no uplift cap is required; absence of a renewal reminder is noted, not flagged.
- **INSURANCE (missing).** No insurance covenant anywhere. We inserted a short paragraph as new Section 10.9 (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, certificates on request).

### Compliant items — no redline

ASSIGN (Section 10.3 imposes no consent requirement and runs to successors and assigns; no change-of-control trigger or HDI re-pricing right), EXCLUSIVITY (at the fallback: defined product category, one-year term, closeout carve-out at 6.2, performance exits at 1.6 and 4.1; Section 6.3 exclusivity runs in our favour), T4C (Section 4.1 no-cause exit on 90 days' notice, at the fallback; HDI's mirror right also 90 days; 1.6 adds a penalty-free exit if the Site is not live in 70 days), GOVLAW (New York law preferred; no arbitration or foreign venue — silence on forum noted as a minor gap), MFN (runs in our favour), MINCOMMIT (revenue share only, first $11,000/month excluded; no minimum, take-or-pay or shortfall, and no volume cap), NOSOLICIT (none in the document; Section 5.4 only appoints General Managers as liaisons).

## Walk-away items

1. **Absence of an IP-infringement indemnity (INDEMN).** HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site and processes customer order data; the total absence of indemnity, defence or hold-harmless language is walk-away territory. Our inserted HDI indemnity must be accepted in substance.
2. **Absence of any insurance covenant (INSURANCE).** HDI hosts the Site on its own server and receives and processes customer order data; no insurance for a data-processing vendor is walk-away territory. Our new Section 10.9 must stand.

We also treat the following as must-fix before signature, given their critical/high severity: the missing limitation of liability (unlimited exposure on both sides), the unallocated ownership of the Site, Content and customer data, and the uncapped one-way Termination Payment in Section 4.2.

## Next steps

1. Send the redlined Agreement to HDI with the four critical/high inserts and edits flagged as priority: HDI indemnity, mutual liability cap with carve-outs, ownership plus licence-back, and the three-month cap on the Section 4.2 Termination Payment.
2. Confirm with the business the reciprocity position on the Termination Payment — HDI owes nothing under 4.2(b) — and whether we will trade anything for the cap.
3. Package the four minimal edits (licence to affiliates/contractors/successors, narrowed 6.1 restraint with carve-outs, once-per-12-months audit cap, 30-day non-renewal window for us) as a single low-friction block.
4. Confirm the operational inputs for the inserted provisions: transition-assistance rates and data-return scope for new Section 4.3, and the insurance limits in new Section 10.9 with our risk team.
5. Optionally raise the minor gaps noted but not flagged: express submission to the New York courts, an independent-auditor requirement in Section 3.4, and a renewal reminder mechanic.
6. Confirm the seven compliant items require no change so the negotiation stays focused on the gaps."}
